# condathis

> Run command line tools in a **reproducible** and **isolated** way,
> right from R.

[`system()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/system.html) calls that work on your
machine often break on others. `condathis` creates self-contained
environments for your command line tools, so your R code runs reliably
for you, your colleagues, and your future self.

## A Quick Example

Two commands install `cowpy` in its own isolated environment and run it:

``` r

# 1. Install 'cowpy' into an environment named 'cowpy-env'
condathis::create_env("cowpy", env_name = "cowpy-env")
#> v Environment cowpy-env successfully created.

# 2. Run it!
# Example showing redirection from a file to the Standard Input (STDIN)
temp_file <- tempfile()
writeLines("{condathis} is awesome!", temp_file)
condathis::run("cowpy", stdin = temp_file, env_name = "cowpy-env")
#>  _________________________
#> < {condathis} is awesome! >
#>  -------------------------
#>      \   ^__^
#>       \  (oo)\_______
#>          (__)\       )\/\
#>            ||----w |
#>            ||     ||
```

For something fancier, use `rich-cli` to format messages:

``` r

condathis::create_env("rich-cli", env_name = "rich-cli-env")
#> v Environment rich-cli-env successfully created.

condathis::run(
  "rich", "[b]Condathis[/b] is awesome!", "-p", "-a", "ascii",
  env_name = "rich-cli-env"
)
#> +-----------------------+
#> | Condathis is awesome! |
#> +-----------------------+
```

You can package any command line tool with your R script, and it runs on
any machine where its packages are available.

## Installation

Install the release version of the package from
[CRAN](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=condathis):

``` r

install.packages("condathis")
```

Or get the development version from
[R-universe](https://luciorq.r-universe.dev/condathis):

``` r

install.packages("condathis", repos = c("https://luciorq.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
```

## Why `condathis`?

R’s [`system()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/system.html) and
[`system2()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/system2.html) depend on tools being
installed on the host system. This creates a few problems:

- **Reproducibility:** Will your script from last year still work? Will
  your collaborator be able to run your code if they have a different
  version of a tool?
- **Conflicts:** What if two different tools need two different versions
  of the same dependency?

`condathis` solves these issues by creating isolated environments for
each tool.

### Reproducibility: An Example

Let’s say you’re using `fastqc` for quality control in a bioinformatics
pipeline. Different versions of `fastqc` can produce slightly different
results.

With `condathis`, you can lock in a specific version:

``` r

fastq_file <- system.file("extdata", "sample1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz", package = "condathis")
temp_out_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "output")
fs::dir_create(temp_out_dir)

# Always use fastqc version 0.12.1
condathis::create_env(
  "fastqc==0.12.1",
  env_name = "fastqc-0.12.1",
  channels = c("conda-forge", "bioconda")
)
#> v Environment fastqc-0.12.1 successfully created.
condathis::run("fastqc", fastq_file, "-o", temp_out_dir, env_name = "fastqc-0.12.1")
#> application/gzip
#> Started analysis of sample1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz
#> Approx 90% complete for sample1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz
#> Analysis complete for sample1_L001_R1_001.fastq.gz
```

Now your analysis uses the same `fastqc` version, regardless of where or
when it runs.

### Isolation: An Example

Need a specific version of a tool like `curl` that is different from the
one your system or R provides?

The `libcurl` that R uses:

``` r

as.character(libcurlVersion())
#> [1] "8.23.0"
```

A specific `curl` version, isolated with `condathis`:

``` r

condathis::create_env(
  "curl==8.10.1",
  env_name = "curl-env"
)
#> v Environment curl-env successfully created.

# Capture the output as an R object, then read its first line
out <- condathis::run(
  "curl", "--version",
  env_name = "curl-env",
  verbose = "silent"
)

condathis::parse_output(out)[1]
#> [1] "curl 8.10.1 (x86_64-conda-linux-gnu) libcurl/8.10.1 OpenSSL/3.6.5 zlib/1.3.2 zstd/1.5.7 libssh2/1.11.1 nghttp2/1.71.0"
```

This lets you run tools with conflicting dependencies side by side.

## How It Works

`condathis` relies on
[**`micromamba`**](https://mamba.readthedocs.io/en/latest/user_guide/micromamba.html)
to bring **reproducibility and isolation**. `micromamba` is a package
manager that “does not need a base environment and does not come with a
default version of Python”. `condathis` uses a usable `micromamba` that
it finds, such as one on your `PATH` (see *micromamba discovery* in
[`` ?condathis::`condathis-options` ``](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/condathis-options.md)).
When it finds none, it downloads one the first time it needs it, so that
first call needs internet access. A message tells you about the download
(class `condathis_micromamba_downloading`), unless `verbose = "silent"`.

`condathis` keeps the downloaded `micromamba`, the package cache and the
environments in its own data directory (see
[`condathis::get_install_dir()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/get_install_dir.md)).
Environments stay there until you remove them.
[`condathis::list_envs()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/list_envs.md)
lists them, `condathis::get_env_dir("cowpy-env")` returns the directory
of one, `condathis::install_packages("jq", env_name = "cowpy-env")` adds
packages to it, `condathis::list_packages("cowpy-env")` lists its
packages, `condathis::remove_env("cowpy-env")` removes it, and
[`condathis::clean_cache()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/clean_cache.md)
deletes the downloaded package files. Removing the `condathis` package
does not delete any of this: the section *Removing everything* of
[`?condathis::clean_cache`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/clean_cache.md)
shows how.

`micromamba` is the built-in *backend* of `condathis`. Other packages
can add backends with the experimental
[`register_backend()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/register_backend.md).
New environments use `micromamba` unless you pass `method` or set
`options(condathis.backend_priority = ...)`. For example,
`method = "rattler"` uses the optional `rattlerthis` package. It is not
on CRAN: it is available from
[R-universe](https://luciorq.r-universe.dev/rattlerthis). The [backends
article](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/articles/backends.html)
shows how to install it and use both backends together.

Already have an environment created outside `condathis`, for example by
`conda`, `mamba`, or `micromamba` itself? Pass its directory as
`env_name = condathis::env_path("/path/to/env")` to
[`run()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run.md),
[`run_bin()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run_bin.md),
[`run_pipeline()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run_pipeline.md)
or
[`run_step()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run_step.md)
to run commands from it. `condathis` never modifies such an environment.
It runs commands in it with `micromamba` by default.

## Output and Errors

`verbose` sets what a call prints:

- `"output"`, the default of the functions that create environments or
  run commands, shows the output of the command and the messages of
  `condathis`.
- `"silent"` shows nothing.
- `"cmd"` shows the command line.
- `"spinner"` shows only a spinner.
- `"full"` shows the command line, the output and the log of the
  backend.

[`run()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run.md) keeps
the output in its result at every level: read it with
[`condathis::parse_output()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/parse_output.md).

A command that fails aborts with an error of class
`condathis_status_error`. Its fields `status`, `stdout` and `stderr`
hold what the command returned. With `error = "continue"`, you get the
result, with its `status`, instead:

``` r

tryCatch(
  condathis::run("curl", "--no-such-option", env_name = "curl-env", verbose = "silent"),
  condathis_status_error = function(e) e$status
)
#> [1] 2

res <- condathis::run(
  "curl", "--no-such-option",
  env_name = "curl-env",
  error = "continue",
  verbose = "silent"
)
res$status
#> [1] 2
```

Every error of `condathis` has the class `condathis_error`, and
[`` ?condathis::`condathis-conditions` ``](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/condathis-conditions.md)
lists the other classes.

## Known Caveats

No shell is involved, so shell syntax in an argument is passed
literally.

- Shell builtins, such as `echo`, are not available as commands. To use
  shell features, run a shell explicitly, for example
  `condathis::run("bash", "-c", "...")`.
- Shell operators such as `|` and `>` are not interpreted.
  - Instead of `>`, use the `stdout`/`stderr` arguments (a file path
    redirects to that file).
  - Instead of `cmd1 | cmd2`, use
    [`condathis::run_pipeline()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run_pipeline.md)
    with one
    [`condathis::run_step()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run_step.md)
    per command, as in
    `run_pipeline(run_step("cmd1"), run_step("cmd2", env_name = "other-env"))`.
    It connects the commands (optionally each in its own Conda
    environment) through operating system pipes. Alternatively, call
    [`condathis::run()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run.md)
    several times and use the `stdout`/`stdin` file arguments to pass
    data between the calls.
  - `stdin` accepts a file path. Set it to `"|"` together with the
    `input` argument to write in-memory data (character or raw vector)
    directly to a command’s standard input. This works with
    [`run()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run.md),
    [`run_bin()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run_bin.md),
    and
    [`run_pipeline()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run_pipeline.md).
- A `~` in a command argument is not expanded.
  - Expand such paths in R, for example with
    [`path.expand()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/path.expand.html) or
    [`fs::path_expand()`](https://fs.r-lib.org/reference/path_expand.html).
  - Relative paths, such as `"data/sample.fastq"` or
    `"../sample.fastq"`, work: they are relative to the working
    directory of R.
- On Windows:
  - Run `cmd.exe` for its builtins, as in
    `condathis::run("cmd", "/c", "dir")`.
  - Batch files (`.bat`, `.cmd`) start through `cmd.exe`, which parses
    their arguments again.
  - `bioconda` has no Windows builds. Its `noarch` packages, such as
    `fastqc`, install on Windows, but tools with compiled code, such as
    `samtools`, need Linux, macOS or the Windows Subsystem for Linux
    (WSL).

## Learn More

- [`vignette("condathis")`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/articles/condathis.md)
  walks through a complete example.
- The [articles](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/articles/) on the
  package website show how to [use Python with
  `reticulate`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/articles/python-and-reticulate.html),
  [stream binary data through
  pipelines](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/articles/whole-slide-images.html),
  and [choose a
  backend](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/articles/backends.html).
- [`?condathis::run`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run.md),
  [`?condathis::run_pipeline`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run_pipeline.md)
  and
  [`?condathis::create_env`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/create_env.md)
  describe every argument.
  [`` ?condathis::`condathis-options` ``](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/condathis-options.md)
  lists the options and environment variables that `condathis` reads.
- Upgrading from 0.1.4? `news(package = "condathis")` lists the breaking
  changes, each with what to write instead.

# Package index

## Run command line tools

Run a command, or a pipeline of commands, in a Conda environment.

- [`run()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run.md) : Run
  a command in a Conda environment
- [`run_bin()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run_bin.md)
  : Run a binary from a Conda environment
- [`run_pipeline()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run_pipeline.md)
  : Run a pipeline of commands connected with pipes
- [`run_step()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/run_step.md)
  : Describe one command of a pipeline
- [`parse_output()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/parse_output.md)
  : Split the output of a command into lines

## Manage environments

Create, change, check, list and remove Conda environments.

- [`create_env()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/create_env.md)
  : Create a Conda environment
- [`install_packages()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/install_packages.md)
  : Install packages in a Conda environment
- [`remove_env()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/remove_env.md)
  : Remove a Conda environment
- [`validate_env()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/validate_env.md)
  : Check that an environment has the requested packages
- [`env_exists()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/env_exists.md)
  : Check whether a Conda environment exists
- [`list_envs()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/list_envs.md)
  : List Conda environments managed by condathis
- [`list_packages()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/list_packages.md)
  : List packages in a Conda environment
- [`get_env_dir()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/get_env_dir.md)
  : Get an environment directory path
- [`env_path()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/env_path.md)
  : Refer to an environment by its path

## Setup: micromamba, data directories and caches

Install and locate the micromamba binary that condathis uses, find the
data directory of each backend, clean the package caches, run code with
temporary home and data directories, and report the operating system and
CPU architecture.

- [`install_micromamba()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/install_micromamba.md)
  : Install micromamba
- [`micromamba_bin_path()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/micromamba_bin_path.md)
  : Get the path of the managed micromamba binary
- [`get_install_dir()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/get_install_dir.md)
  : Get the data directories of the backends
- [`clean_cache()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/clean_cache.md)
  : Clean the package caches of condathis
- [`with_sandbox_dir()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/with_sandbox_dir.md)
  : Run code with temporary home and data directories
- [`get_sys_arch()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/get_sys_arch.md)
  : Get operating system and CPU architecture

## Backends

Add, remove and inspect backends that create and run environments.

- [`register_backend()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/register_backend.md)
  : Register a condathis backend
- [`unregister_backend()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/unregister_backend.md)
  : Unregister a condathis backend
- [`list_registered_backend_names()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/list_registered_backend_names.md)
  : List the registered backends
- [`backend_root_dir()`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/backend_root_dir.md)
  : Get the root directory of a backend

## Options and conditions

The options and environment variables that condathis reads or sets, and
the classes of the conditions it signals.

- [`condathis-options`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/condathis-options.md)
  [`condathis_options`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/condathis-options.md)
  : Options and environment variables used by condathis
- [`condathis-conditions`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/condathis-conditions.md)
  [`condathis_conditions`](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/reference/condathis-conditions.md)
  : Condition classes of condathis

# Articles

### Worked examples

- [Running Python Code with condathis and
  reticulate](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/articles/python-and-reticulate.md):

  Run Python as a command line tool, or embed it in R with reticulate,
  from one Conda environment.

- [Whole-Slide Pathology Images: Binary Pipelines Across
  Environments](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/articles/whole-slide-images.md):

  Stream binary image data through a pipeline whose commands run in
  different environments.

### Backends

- [Backends: micromamba and
  rattler](https://luciorq.github.io/condathis/articles/backends.md):

  Choose the engine that creates and runs your Conda environments, and
  use the rattler backend of rattlerthis next to micromamba.
